match.reason: Neither bank point teaches graph types (connected, isomorphic, loops, multiple edges) or the adjacency matrix; the logarithm card and the trees card cover different ideas.

draft.title: Types of graphs and the adjacency matrix
card: a graph where you can get from any vertex to any other by following edges. If one vertex is cut off, the graph is not connected.
a loop is an edge that starts and ends at the same vertex. Multiple edges are two or more edges joining the same pair of vertices.
two graphs are isomorphic if they have the same structure: the same number of vertices and the same connections, even if they are drawn differently.

a square table with one row and one column for each vertex. The entry is the number of edges joining the row vertex to the column vertex. A loop counts as 1 in this course. Example: if A and B are joined by 2 edges, both the A-B and B-A entries are 2.
draft.remember: An adjacency matrix counts the edges between each pair of vertices, and it is the same either side of the diagonal.

a.q: A graph has vertices A, B and C. A and B are joined by one edge, and B and C are joined by two edges. What is the entry in row C, column B of its adjacency matrix?
a.why: Row C, column B counts the edges joining C and B, which is 2. The answer 1 comes from counting the A-B edge or from treating multiple edges as one connection.
a.clue: Count every edge between C and B.

b.q: Mia draws a graph with 4 vertices. Vertex P has a loop and one edge to Q. Q has one edge to R. R has one edge to S. What is the sum of all the entries in its adjacency matrix?
b.why: Each of the 3 edges between different vertices appears twice in the matrix, giving 6. The loop is entered once, as 1, so the total is 7. Answering 6 forgets the loop, and 8 counts the loop twice.
b.clue: Edges between two vertices appear on both sides of the diagonal.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: row C, column B is 2, and the matrix total is 7, using the VCE convention that a loop counts as 1.
